run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-15T10:48:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Two pods in namespace otel-demo are Pending — ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh — and they are the only Pending pods in the cluster. Both are surge replicas created by a deployment rollout at 10:47:30Z/10:47:38Z, about a minute before the alert start of 2026-11-15T10:48:27Z, and both are unschedulable because their pod templates pin spec.nodeSelector to kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node, a value no node carries. The scheduler's message is '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.' The bad selector is present on the ad and cart Deployments themselves (generation 2, helm release revision 2) and on no other deployment in the cluster; it was introduced when those two deployments were updated, producing new ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5. The prior ReplicaSet pods (ad-554b849958-42mdm, cart-755465879b-bgb2p) are still Running and Ready with 0 restarts and remain the sole Endpoints for the ad and cart Services, so no ad/cart error-rate increase was observed (ad error spans 1.05 in the 15m post-window vs 2.06 in the prior 15m baseline; cart 0 in both); the observable damage is the stuck rollout and two permanently unschedulable replicas. Who or what wrote the invalid-node value cannot be verified because change history is not integrated and Helm release data is unreadable.

claims.text: Exactly two pods in namespace otel-demo are Pending: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; the other 21 pods in the namespace are Running.

Both Pending pods have PodScheduled condition status False with reason Unschedulable and message '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' Repeated FailedScheduling warning events from kube-scheduler are recorded for both pods between 2026-11-15T10:47:30Z and 2026-11-15T10:57:53Z.

Both Pending pods specify spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}, have no nodeName and no container statuses, and are owned by ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 and ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 respectively.

No node carries kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node: the 5 nodes' kubernetes.io/hostname label values are i-01a47734339426210, i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba. Four worker nodes are Ready with 4 CPU and about 16Gi memory allocatable and no taints; only i-01a47734339426210 has the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule taint.

The pod templates of Deployment ad and Deployment cart themselves contain nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node; both are at generation 2 with annotations deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2 and meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo. They are the only deployments in the whole cluster with that selector (other deployments with a nodeSelector use kubernetes.io/os=linux).

ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 was created at 2026-11-15T10:47:30Z and ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 at 2026-11-15T10:47:38Z, both with nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node and no available or ready replicas. Events show the controllers' SuccessfulCreate of pods ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 'from 0 to 1' for both ReplicaSets at those same timestamps.

The previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 (created 2026-11-15T10:10:05Z) and cart-755465879b (10:10:04Z) have nodeSelector null and each still runs one ready pod: ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p are Running and Ready with restartCount 0. Both Deployments therefore report status replicas 2, availableReplicas 1, readyReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 and unavailableReplicas 1 with condition Available/MinimumReplicasAvailable True.

Service endpoints remain populated by the old pods: the ad Endpoints subset has ready address 100.96.3.180:8080 and cart has ready address 100.96.3.205:8080, with no notReadyAddresses for either; the Services select opentelemetry.io/name=ad and opentelemetry.io/name=cart on port 8080.
No ResourceQuota objects exist in namespace otel-demo (the query over kind resourcequotas returned no items), so quota admission is not what limits these pods.
Only two Pending pods exist in the entire cluster at query time, both in otel-demo (otel-demo/ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and otel-demo/cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh).

ad and cart trace error counts did not increase across the change: in the 15m window 10:48-11:03 ad had 1.05 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in 1423.2 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans and cart had 0 error spans in 13033.1 spans; in the comparable 15m baseline 10:32-10:47 ad had 2.06 error spans in 1769.4 spans and cart 0 error spans in 15332.3 spans.

The ad and cart Deployments are not currently unavailable: both report availableReplicas 1 and Available/MinimumReplicasAvailable True, their Services have ready endpoints, and their error-span rate is not elevated relative to the pre-change baseline, so no customer-facing outage of ad or cart was observed from this misconfiguration.

Node resource exhaustion, memory/disk/PID pressure, or namespace quota as the reason the pods cannot schedule: the scheduler message names only an untolerated control-plane taint and node affinity/selector mismatches with 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', all four worker nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False, and no ResourceQuota exists in otel-demo.

The control-plane NoSchedule taint as the cause of the Pending pods: that taint excludes only 1 of 5 nodes, while the scheduler reports the other 4 nodes were excluded because they 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', and no node carries a matching kubernetes.io/hostname value.

The trigger for the alert is the deployment update applied to ad and cart around 2026-11-15T10:47:30Z-10:47:38Z (deployment generation and helm revision 2, release otel-demo) that added nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node to their pod templates; the RollingUpdate created surge replicas that can never schedule because the selector matches no node, while the old ReplicaSet pods keep serving. Who or what performed that change is not verifiable from the available sources.

Latent risk (unverified): each of ad and cart now has a single schedulable replica. If the old pod ad-554b849958-42mdm or cart-755465879b-bgb2p is deleted, evicted or rescheduled, its replacement from the current ReplicaSet cannot schedule under nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node, which would make that Deployment unavailable. No such deletion or unavailability was observed in this window.

Correct the pod template nodeSelector on Deployment ad and Deployment cart in otel-demo — remove kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node or set it to a real node hostname label — and re-apply (for example, correct the otel-demo helm values and upgrade). The two stuck ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 should then schedule and the old ReplicaSets roll down; verify with PodScheduled conditions and Deployment unavailableReplicas.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, and Helm release data lives in Secrets that cannot be read, so who or what set kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node on ad and cart (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2, meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo) could not be verified; the deployment generation and annotations only show that a revision-2 change exists.

Prometheus metric-name discovery for kube_pod_status*/kube_resourcequota*/kube_pod_container_status* returned no_data (6c296892-fbf7-4cf0-9420-22f483f05131-t0:c264fb0c-62ef-4752-8951-df56b703c43b) and the kube_deployment_status.*/kube_pod_.* discovery also returned no_data (2aed69aa-2a9e-4e8f-8d1e-e9369a780671-t0:144fa34a-c25f-47c7-90c3-b0e56ef6f6b1), and the instant query kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo",deployment=~"ad|cart"} returned no_data (dc657e48-614c-4225-8d60-92c6b6e4af7e-t0:7e5c1605-346d-4570-85fa-a36c31ed54a7); the Pending-pod count and Deployment availability could therefore not be charted over time, and missing series are unknown rather than zero. The Pending interval is inferred only from pod/ReplicaSet creation and first FailedScheduling event timestamps (2026-11-15T10:47:30Z and 10:47:38Z).

list_prometheus_rules with rule_name PendingPodsDetected returned no_data (684df9fa-6c68-41c8-ac22-91c24c961e64-t0:e6065cec-7bf5-4401-84fd-1a0ac132f79e), so the alert's exact expression and evaluation state in this Prometheus could not be confirmed; the alert payload (current: 2) matches the 2 Pending pods observed, but the rule itself was not found here.

The traces_search_by_tags query for service ad with error=true returned no_data (8c2a312f-d057-4e37-84a1-68255c29d232-t1:03172595-ae7a-4b98-9788-0c100fa5854c), so per-span error detail for ad was not obtained; ad error-rate conclusions rest on the aggregated span metrics.

The error-filtered log reads for the running pods returned no_data (ad-554b849958-42mdm: f1b91b1e-3a97-43f5-b8d6-aeb32cb968ae-t1:a15497c9-0709-465d-a615-7f9fd07ede70 with 3952 lines read; cart-755465879b-bgb2p: f1b91b1e-3a97-43f5-b8d6-aeb32cb968ae-t2:3887363f-0337-4dbb-9166-c40d264ee3bb with 12736 lines read), so the absence of application error lines is not proven; health of the old pods rests on Running/Ready state, restartCount 0, endpoints and error-span rates.

Kubernetes objects reflect cluster state at query time (about 2026-11-15T11:03-11:04Z), not at 10:48Z: it is not directly observable whether the invalid nodeSelector already existed before object revision 2 or whether other pods were Pending earlier in the window.

No evidence was gathered on which downstream callers (for example frontend or checkout) were affected by the stuck ad/cart rollout, and no such impact was observed in ad or cart themselves; the impact assessment stops at the deployment and pod layer.
next_steps: Inspect the otel-demo Helm values and release in the change-management system (not available here) to find where nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node was introduced for the ad and cart components and whether other manifest sources would re-apply it.
After correcting the selector, confirm both new pods reach PodScheduled=True and Running, and that Deployment ad and cart show unavailableReplicas 0 with the old ReplicaSets scaled to 0.

Consider tightening the PendingPodsDetected alert with a pod-age threshold or a rollout-stuck condition so a permanently unschedulable surge replica is distinguished from a transient scheduling delay.
